patch.value: A truncated list-all answer is consumed as if it were complete

All three list-all call sites (loadKeyIndex for upsert key matching, loadAppliedByTransaction for atomic-import resume scans, buildCsvExport for CSV export) read .items from the pm list-all --json envelope without checking the envelope's completeness receipt. Verified on this host against the 682-item workspace: pm 2026.8.14 returned 10 items with truncated=true, so a CSV export silently shipped 10 of 682 rows reporting success, a resume scan silently saw none of the applied rows (re-importing on resume), and an upsert key index silently missed keys (creating duplicates). 2026.8.15 fixes the default, but truncated can still go true under an output budget and completeness.status can go partial when items are unreadable — each must refuse loudly instead of producing a partial answer that reports success. Related: @unbrained/pm-cli resolves through floating ranges (^2026.8.6 dev, >=2026.8.3 peer), which is how the 2026.8.14 regression reached this package with no diff to review.

All three list-all call sites now parse the full envelope and refuse an incomplete answer via assertListAllComplete, which trips on truncated, has_more, completeness.status other than complete, or omission_receipt.has_omissions, naming the tripped signal and the count-versus-total figures. No --limit is passed on any list-all read. The pm CLI is exact-pinned at 2026.8.15 in devDependencies with a >=2026.8.15 peer floor.

A truncated or degraded list-all envelope causes the command to fail loudly rather than producing a partial CSV export, a resume scan that re-imports applied rows, or an upsert key index that creates duplicates.

149 of 149 tests pass with the gate in place. Neutering assertListAllComplete to a no-op and rebuilding fails 7 tests, so the refusals are exercised rather than asserted vacuously. Verified against the real 2026.8.15 envelope on this host: count 682, total 682, truncated false, completeness.status complete.
